problem: Dense semantic annotation of indoor scenes is slow and costly, and fixed-vocabulary segmentation models miss long-tail indoor objects. Zero-shot CLIP/LSeg-based navigation (e.g., VLMaps) localizes objects poorly.
motivation: Embodied agents need to detect many small, long-tail indoor objects, but labeling datasets like HM3D took over 14,200 human hours. Foundation models (SAM, Detic, MaskFormer) are complementary: SAM gives accurate boundaries, Detic gives open-vocabulary foreground objects, MaskFormer gives background regions. Fusing them, plus multi-view consistency, should give cheap pseudo-labels that beat holistic vision-language embeddings for semantic goal navigation.
key_idea: Fuse SAM boundaries with MaskFormer (background) and Detic (LVIS foreground objects) for single-view pseudo-labels, then refine with multi-view voting using depth and poses, and use the labels to build semantic maps for navigation.
insight: Boundaries from SAM improve mIoU, especially on small objects (AVD mIoU-small 60.2 to 70.7 with SAM, 92.8 with Detic, 97.7 with multi-view verification). Multi-view voting fixes single-view errors from occlusion and odd viewpoints. Semantic maps built from fused labels give better goal localization than LSeg embedding dot-products (89.4 vs 78.9 SR), but that comparison uses labels produced on the same scenes with the full trajectory available.
method: Semantic segmentation with SAM: prompt SAM with a 64x64 dense point grid, then assign each segment the MaskFormer (ADE20K) class with the most pixel votes.

Detic+SAM foreground instances: Detic with the LVIS vocabulary (1203 classes) gives boxes, which are refined by prompting SAM with the box and the mask centroid. Manual boxes, if available, are handled the same way.
Overlay fusion: keep only floor, ceiling, door, blind and wall from MaskFormer, then superimpose the Detic+SAM foreground masks on top.

Multi-view verification: back-project annotations of two nearby reference frames into 3D using depth and pose, reproject onto the target frame with depth-consistency filtering, and vote per connected-component region. The vote averages the two normalized reference scores and the frame's own score of 1, and the highest class wins.
Part discovery: take SAM segments inside Detic 'cabinet' boxes, extract ResNet-50 RoIAlign features, run per-scene k-means (3-5 clusters), and manually pick the handle cluster.
Semantic map for ObjectNav (GT-Maps): project labels to a 3D point cloud, voxelize, and take the top-down majority class per 5cm cell. Localize the goal on the map and plan with A*.

setting.backbone: SAM + Detic (LVIS) + MaskFormer (ADE20K), all frozen; ResNet-50 features for part clustering; LSeg for VLMaps baseline
setting.observation: RGB-D images with camera poses (Active Vision Dataset, Kinect V2)
setting.action_space: move to neighboring cell on navigation grid + STOP
setting.simulator: none; AVD real-scan dataset, navigation grid over captured views
setting.privileged: Robot can traverse the entire scene before navigating to build the semantic map (pre-exploration); depth and poses given; manually inspected success

numbers.eval_set_note: 19 scenes with random goals per run (paper says 20 episodes per run, 3 seeds R1-R3), manually judged success
numbers.extra: Pre-explored full scene map; uses RGB-D, poses, and auto-labeled segmentation; SR judged by manual inspection
numbers.evidence: Table 2 Object Goal Navigation Results: GT-Maps 94.7 / 78.9 / 94.7, Avg-SR 89.4±9.1

numbers.eval_set_note: 200 manually labeled images (first 10 per scene, 20 scenes)

numbers_note: Only the navigation experiment is a navigation benchmark; it is a custom AVD setup, not a standard one. Table 1 also reports single-view AVD-GT numbers (64.2 / 92.8).
results: Fused labels raise ADE20K-indoor mIoU from 55.7 (MaskFormer) to 58.3, and AVD-GT small-object mIoU from 60.2 to 97.7 with multi-view verification. On AVD object goal navigation, GT-Maps reaches 89.4% average SR vs 78.9% for VLMaps (LSeg), about +10.5 points.
limitations: Navigation evaluation is small (about 20 episodes x 3 runs), custom, judged manually, and assumes full prior traversal of the scene to build the map
Labeling is compute-heavy (about 120 GPU-hours on two A100s for AVD), and multi-view verification needs depth and poses
On AVD, MaskFormer+SAM slightly outperforms adding Detic in overall mIoU (64.9 vs 64.2), and part discovery needs manual cluster selection
